hero.subtitle: Our goal is for your family to stay together, and for your child to stay home. We work toward it with a Child and Family Team, one Care Plan, and the ten principles California requires.

gettingStarted.title: How do I get started with Love Pathways Wraparound?
gettingStarted.quote: "We consider it a successful outcome when the family feels empowered."

requestSupport.title: Request Support
requestSupport.desc: Wraparound services can be requested by members of the immediate family.

completeForm.title: Complete Initial Form
completeForm.desc: Once the initial form is completed, a representative will be in touch to discuss the program and explain the requirements.

consultation.title: Initial Consultation
consultation.desc: We'll discuss your specific situation and how the Fear to Love model, developed by Bryan Post, can best support your family.

phases.title: The 4 Phases of Wraparound Care
phases.intro: Following your initial consultation, our High Fidelity Wraparound model kicks in. We use four distinct phases to guide and support your family's journey toward independence.
phases.label: Phase

engagement.title: Engagement
engagement.desc: Focused on listening to your story, building trust, and identifying your support team.

planDevelopment.title: Plan Development
planDevelopment.desc: Building your personalized care plan around your culture and unique strengths.

implementation.title: Implementation
implementation.desc: Putting the plan into action, with ongoing progress monitoring and adjustments made with your team.

transition.title: Transition
transition.desc: Preparing for independence through community integration and stronger natural supports.

reach.description: We deliver in-home Wraparound services across 10 counties in California's Central Valley and Bay Area, so no adoptive family has to walk their journey alone.
reach.cardDescription: Our mission is to reach every family in need. If your county is not on this list, please reach out. We are constantly evaluating new areas to bring Wraparound support where it is needed most.
reach.mapTitle: Map of the 10 California counties served by Love Pathways Wraparound
reach.mapDesc: Love Pathways Wraparound serves families across 10 counties in California. Each served county is filled in and marked with a pin.

team.intro: High Fidelity Wraparound puts a team around your family instead of sending your child somewhere else. Preventing that placement disruption is the whole point of Wraparound. Some of the team is ours. Some of it is yours.

facilitator.title: Facilitator
facilitator.desc: Leads the team and keeps the Care Plan aligned with what your family said it wants.

specialist.title: Family Specialist
specialist.desc: Works directly with your family between meetings, in your home and in your community.

parentPartner.title: Parent Partner
parentPartner.desc: A parent who has been through this, sitting on your side of the table.

yourPeople.title: The People You Choose
yourPeople.desc: A grandmother, a neighbor, a coach, a teacher. Anyone who matters to your child can be on the team.

principles.intro: California’s Wraparound Standards define high fidelity as adherence to four phases and the 10 principles of the National Wraparound Initiative, which the state adopted. Not marketing language, a state standard. Here is what each of the ten principles means for your family.

p1.name: Family Voice and Choice
p1.desc: You and your family have a say in the decisions made. Your ideas, opinions and preferences guide the plan.
p1.example: A Facilitator makes sure a mother’s wish to include a trusted relative in her child’s care plan is honored.

p2.name: Strengths-Based
p2.desc: We focus on what your family does well, and use those strengths to solve challenges instead of only looking at problems.
p2.example: A Family Specialist notices a child’s artistic ability and builds it into the plan as a way to express difficult feelings.

p3.name: Individualized
p3.desc: Every family is different, and so is every plan. Yours is made only for you, for your specific needs.
p3.example: A behavior plan for a child with ADHD is built around daily routines and accommodations that fit that child, not a template.

p4.name: Natural Supports
p4.desc: We help you bring people from your own life into the Care Plan: friends, relatives, neighbors who can be part of your team.
p4.example: A family reconnects with a supportive neighbor who becomes part of the care team and keeps helping long after the program ends.

p5.name: Community-Based
p5.desc: Support happens where you live, not only in an office. That keeps you connected and makes the help easier to accept.
p5.example: A mentor from the local youth center meets with the child in a place the child already knows.

p6.name: Culturally Respectful and Relevant
p6.desc: Your family’s culture, traditions and beliefs are part of the plan, not an exception to it.
p6.example: The plan is built around the family’s own celebrations and rituals rather than asking them to set those aside.

p7.name: Team-Based
p7.desc: You are not alone. Your team includes people who care about you and professionals who coordinate with each other.
p7.example: Teachers, therapists and family members meet as one Child and Family Team instead of each working separately.

p8.name: Collaboration
p8.desc: Everyone shares ideas and decisions, so nothing pulls in two directions at once.
p8.example: In a team meeting, the Parent Partner makes sure the family’s view is weighed alongside the professionals’ recommendations.

p9.name: Outcomes-Based
p9.desc: Clear goals, tracked. If something is not working, the plan changes.
p9.example: The team reviews school attendance every month and adjusts the plan when the numbers say it is not working.

p10.name: Persistence
p10.desc: Setbacks mean the plan needs adjusting, not that your family failed. Your team stays.
p10.example: After a hard month the team keeps showing up, changing the plan rather than closing the case.

funding.label: Funding and cost
funding.lead: There is no cost to your family.
funding.cost: The Adoption Assistance Program (AAP) funds this Wraparound program, so there is no out-of-pocket cost to your family, nothing is billed to you, and nothing varies by the services your child needs.
funding.legal: California High Fidelity Wraparound is authorized under SB 163, codified in Welfare and Institutions Code 18250 to 18258.
